progress.text: File › Recover follows the app theme (#3243, part of #2348): no black page or forced white text on the light theme

Restrict Editing: with Filling in forms enforced, inserting content controls, their Properties and Remove Content Control are refused, as in Word (it greys them out), so a form's fields stay as they are and only their content is filled in.

Content controls: text typed over a placeholder takes the control's own run properties (w:sdtPr/w:rPr, ECMA-376 §17.5.2.27), as in Word, and the placeholder style is recognised by its built-in name "Placeholder Text" whatever its localized id (German Word: Platzhaltertext), so entries in forms from localized Word no longer stay grey.

Save As, Export and Open no longer do nothing on Linux desktops whose file chooser portal fails to show its dialog (#2999): a "cancel" quicker than anyone could make one asks again without the parent window, then opens the built-in file browser.
Long navigation headings wrap onto further lines inside the resizable pane instead of ending in an ellipsis: the row grows with the text and the pane keeps its width (#759, #3015).

Clearing a font query with no matches keeps Recently Used Fonts visible at the top of a scrollable list. The initial scroll position no longer skips its heading; measured keyboard scrolling is unchanged (#2068).

Symbols keep their font (#2036): a w:sym or Insert › Symbol character in Wingdings, Symbol or Webdings remembers its symbol font apart from the text's font, so selecting all and changing the font (or Clear Formatting) no longer turns the symbols into boxes; saved back to DOCX as w:sym, so Word shows them too. Typed text and the Format Painter don't pick up the symbol font.

Manage Sources › Import… (#2640) reads a Word bibliography file (b:Sources: Word's own Sources.xml master list) into the document: the tags, names, kinds and fields Word saves are read by the same code that reads the bibliography custom XML part of a .docx, a tag already in the document is left alone (an import never overwrites an edited source), an untagged source gets a tag the way a new one does, the whole import is one undo step, and a file that isn't b:Sources is refused.

Picture Format › Size (#2573): width and height in the interface unit, and a size typed in any unit works, pixels too (300 px keeps the picture's proportions, #1901), applied once typed (Enter, Tab or a click elsewhere; Esc cancels) in one undo step. The group's launcher opens a Size dialog: height and width, scale of the original size (or of the size it opened with), Lock aspect ratio, the original size with its pixels, and Reset. picture.size {"original": true, "scale"?} sizes from the original; sizes past 4000 pt that keep the proportions shrink as a whole.

Split Cells and Convert Text to Table dialogs (#2592), matched to Word: Split Cells starts from the selection (twice its columns, its rows; Merge cells before split offered for several cells or one cell merged across columns); table.split gains rows and mergeFirst, a merged cell splits into 1 to its height rows (its height cuts it into rows, 1 × 1 changes nothing, a number that doesn't divide the height or more than it is refused with Word's messages) and column splits make equal parts without moving other rows' grid lines. Convert Text to Table guesses columns live, shows the row count, and offers Initial column width (Auto or up to 22 in, kept as each column's preferred width), AutoFit to contents/window and Paragraphs/Commas/Tabs/Other separators; table.fromText gains paragraph/other + char, columns, autofit and width.

Different First Page works from page 1 (#2826): Insert › Header and Edit Header with the caret on page 1, and a double-click there while another header is being edited, go into page 1's own header instead of the default one page 1 no longer shows.

Edit Recipient List finds records (#1576): a Find in list box hides rows with no cell containing the text (any case) and counts the matches, and "Show only records that will be merged" hides the rows the filter leaves out; both only change the view. Rows are striped, and edits and removes go to the right record however the grid is narrowed

Restrict Editing holds for structure too (#1327): an exception inside a table cell no longer lets table, row or cell formatting change the protected rest of the table; formatting limited to styles refuses Paste Formatting, table shading, borders, cell alignment, cell margins, text direction, table-style edits and locked table styles; loading, filtering or sorting recipients no longer rewrites merge-field results in a protected document.

Ribbon hover hints: a disabled control says why (the command's own reason), split-button arrows, menu buttons and the font, size and outline boxes have hints, and hints show on keyboard focus (#1086).
Insert › Drop Cap is a menu (None, Dropped, In margin, Drop Cap Options…); the dialog sets position, font, lines to drop and distance; letters in the margin; DOCX keeps them (#2601).
SECTIONPAGES includes shared continuous-section pages. A native original control confirms a section starting on page 1 and continuing on page 2 reports 2.

File › Print's Scale to paper size (#2108): pick Letter, Legal, A4 or any Layout › Size paper and every page is scaled to it and centred, the paper turned to each page's orientation, in the preview, the print job (with the spooler's media) and Save these pages as PDF; the document keeps its page size. paper param on ui.print/file.printPdf
Non-overlapping body floating tables clear header tables. Original native controls distinguish never-overlap from allowed overlap.

Paste from LibreOffice: a paragraph indented on both sides (HTML <blockquote> on the clipboard) pastes as an indented Normal paragraph with LibreOffice's margins, not centred and italic in the Quote style (#1270).
DrawingML shape outlines retain explicit preset/custom dashes on screen and in PDF, including zero-width path strokes.
Missing Arial Unicode MS tries Arial and its proportional substitutes before code-font heuristics.

DOCX glossary documents (building blocks) open into the model: Insert › Quick Parts and AutoText list and insert the document's own entries, and saving an entry with "in": "document" keeps it in the file (undoable). An untouched glossary is saved back byte for byte; an edited one is written from the model
A table inserted in a right-to-left paragraph is a right-to-left table, like Word, so Tab moves right to left through its cells (#2634)
Language dialog keeps inherited proofing language and no-proof choices (#2717). Opening and accepting unchanged no longer replaces style-derived values with English US and proofing enabled.

Saving into a folder that refuses a temporary file (macOS privacy protection, read-only folders, #2138) never overwrites an existing document in place: it is left untouched and the error says to use Save As to another folder or allow WordCraft access to the folder (System Settings › Privacy & Security › Files and Folders on macOS). A new file is created directly. Unit tests on Linux; not yet confirmed on a Mac

wordcraft-cli run --script FILE.json (- for stdin) runs a JSON list of commands, then saves to one or more outputs (docx and pdf in one run); errors name the command number and id and nothing is saved, #1963

Strict OOXML line heights render as Word renders them (#2329): w:line="13.90pt" under lineRule="auto" is a height read through twips (13.90 × 20 = 278; the 1.1583 multiple Word shows), not the 13.9 multiple the bare transitional number counts, so a Word 2024 file with 13.9 lines of line spacing opens at Word's 1 page with matching baselines instead of 10

The Spike, as in Word: Ctrl+F3 (⌘F3 on macOS) cuts the selection and adds it to the end of the Spike, each piece followed by a paragraph mark; Ctrl+Shift+F3 (⌘⇧F3) inserts everything collected, in order and with its formatting, and empties the Spike. The clipboard is left alone; each is one undo step. The Spike is the AutoText entry "Spike", so Insert › Quick Parts inserts it without emptying it. It lasts for the session (Word keeps it in Normal.dotm)
Update Field is offered on a table of contents after a save and reopen, and repeated save and update adds no blank line (#2182; the flow in that report already worked since #1197)

DOCX two lines in one and horizontal in vertical (w:eastAsianLayout: id, combine, brackets, vert, vertCompress) are read and kept on save, in runs and character styles, instead of being dropped. Layout doesn't apply them yet.

Read Aloud speaks Russian, Ukrainian, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, CJK and Thai text with a voice for its language instead of spelling out letters (#1843): the sentence's language comes from its run's tag (w:bidi for right-to-left text) or, when that disagrees with the script, from its letters, even when English letters outnumber them; Windows reads the text as UTF-8 and picks an installed voice of that language, macOS say -v and Linux espeak -v get the same language. The user's own voice stays whenever it already speaks the language (English documents read exactly as before), and a voice espeak lacks falls back to the default voice instead of silence. Not run on Windows or macOS here.
Hint-reliant CJK fonts execute TrueType contour assembly; Windows DFKai-SB no longer loses strokes. Synthetic local-font regression; no font binaries bundled.
Ctrl/⌘+wheel only zooms: a coast or wheel notch still gliding no longer scrolls the page on top of the zoom, which keeps the page point under the pointer (#1743).
Releasing a table drag with the mouse (column or row border, move handle, selection areas) leaves the view where it is instead of scrolling back to the caret (#1738)

Hebrew in fields and quotes (#1670): a STYLEREF (or any field) showing right-to-left text such as "פרק א" reads right to left in headers and the body instead of reversed; smart quotes in Hebrew pinned to Word's logical-order result (“ before, ” after, ” in acronyms like צה"ל)
Zero-extent drawing anchors contribute no inline font height.

Control-channel keyboard and text input reaches the focused widget while the native window is inactive, without activating it; normal widget targets, dialogs and document protection remain in force (#2420)
Footnote and endnote editing keeps the body and active note text at normal opacity (#2545), without changing document colours or print/PDF output.

A picture watermark in a header that starts with a table is drawn centred on the page behind the body text, on every page, instead of in the header's cell at the top of the page (#1775); layoutInCell="0" and VML o:allowincell="f" survive save and reopen
An otherwise empty section starting a new page retains its paragraph line before a continuous section, matching an original native Word control.
